Their school project has wings. ✈️🔧

Students at Manchester School of Technology in New Hampshire have completed their second airplane: a two-seat Van’s RV-12iS.

The Aviation Museum of New Hampshire’s October 20 update celebrates the October 10 ribbon-cutting at Manchester-Boston Regional Airport. The build took three school years, with students working alongside volunteer mentors under aviation instructor Jeff Sullivan.

Former student Katrina Maglio, who helped build the airplane and now works for Signature Aviation at the airport, spoke at the ceremony—a connection between classroom skills and an aviation workplace.

The museum says final testing is still ahead before partner Tango Flight sells the aircraft. Meanwhile, students and mentors are already working on airplane number three.

That’s hands-on general aviation: learning the tools, solving problems and seeing years of teamwork become an airplane. Here’s to the students and mentors making it happen. 💙
